answer: An attacker who floods the jury with fake votes also floods itself with the cost of its own dishonest votes, because every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer. The reason this works is that the attacker must pay a real cost on every identity, so scale becomes a liability rather than an advantage. The practical consequence is a steady economy where reputation is earned slowly, spent carefully, and never inflated by a sudden influx of cheap accounts. Consider a wharf as the anchor of the cost. A dawn stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a basalt holds the reputation...
